name: Hexarelin

b.x: Growth hormone release about twice that of GHRH at the same IV dose. Ghigo and colleagues measured this in 12 healthy young volunteers, with a dose-dependent response after subcutaneous injection too [1]. GHRP-2 matched hexarelin's GH pulse at equal IV doses in two head-to-head studies [3] [9]. Hexarelin is a synthetic hexapeptide GHS-R1a agonist, sometimes listed under CAS 140703-51-1, that mimics ghrelin at both the pituitary and hypothalamus to trigger growth hormone release. Hexarelin also binds a second target, the CD36 scavenger receptor. Bodart and colleagues found this second binding site in rat heart tissue in 1999 [2] and identified it as CD36 in 2002 [7]. Through CD36, hexarelin produces anti-fibrotic cardiac effects and preserves cell contractility during ischemia, completely independent of the GH axis. Other GHRPs share this dual profile. A 2017 review describes the GHRP family as binding both GHS-R1a and CD36 [12]. The practical reality is a 4-week ceiling. Hexarelin's high GHS-R1a binding affinity drives receptor downregulation faster than any other peptide in this class. Community protocols converge on 4 weeks on, 2 to 4 weeks off, with many users adding 5-on/2-off weekly cycling within each block to slow desensitization further. The typical stack pairs 100 to 200 mcg hexarelin with 100 mcg CJC-1295 (no DAC) co-injected subcutaneously at bedtime. About 311 PubMed papers cover hexarelin. Most are mechanistic or short-term pharmacological work, not long-term therapeutic trials. It reached Phase II for adult GH deficiency and heart failure before development was abandoned, likely because desensitization made chronic dosing impractical. It was never submitted for FDA approval and remains a research-only compound. Community experience across dozens of Reddit threads tracks closely with the published pharmacology; the 100 to 200 mcg per injection dosing range is where most users land.

Hexarelin binds GHS-R1a at the anterior pituitary with higher affinity than any other growth hormone releasing peptide. That binding triggers a calcium-dependent signaling cascade in somatotroph cells, producing a GH pulse within 30 minutes of subcutaneous injection. Unlike ipamorelin, which is selective for GHS-R1a, hexarelin also activates ACTH release from the pituitary. This cross-reactivity explains the cortisol and prolactin elevations that Arvat and colleagues measured in healthy adults [3]. GHRP-2 at matched doses raised them by similar amounts in the same study. The second receptor is what sets hexarelin apart. Bodart's group identified CD36, a scavenger receptor expressed on cardiomyocytes, as a direct hexarelin binding target [7]. Through CD36, hexarelin reduces cardiac fibrosis, preserves cell shortening during ischemia-reperfusion injury, and regulates intracellular calcium handling. A 2018 mouse study confirmed that hexarelin treatment preserves myocardial function and reduces fibrosis after acute myocardial infarction [4]. These cardiac effects operate entirely independently of GH release. Plasma half-life runs approximately 55 to 70 minutes after subcutaneous injection, with GH peak occurring around 30 minutes post-dose. Oral bioavailability is only about 0.3%, making subcutaneous injection the only practical route. The short half-life means each injection produces a discrete GH pulse rather than sustained elevation; that pulsatile pattern mimics natural physiology better than continuous GH administration.
Hexarelin benefits center on short-cycle GH output and a cardiac mechanism through the CD36 receptor.
Releases about twice the GH of GHRH at the same IV dose [1], and the response nears its ceiling at 1 to 2 mcg/kg IV [5]. GHRP-2 matched it head to head at equal IV doses [3] [9].

Binds the CD36 cardiac receptor independently of GH release. Mouse models show preserved myocardial function and reduced fibrosis after acute infarction [4]. Other GHRPs bind CD36 too, per a 2017 review of the peptide family [12].

Sleep architecture improves with bedtime dosing. GH promotes slow-wave sleep, and community reports consistently flag deeper sleep as one of the first noticeable effects within the opening 2 to 3 doses.
Complementary with GHRH peptides through dual receptor activation. Pairing hexarelin (GHS-R1a) with CJC-1295 no DAC (GHRHR) produces a GH pulse larger than either compound alone.
Body recomposition signal within a 4-week window. Users report reduced abdominal fat and improved muscle fullness by weeks 3 to 4, particularly at the intermediate 200 mcg twice daily protocol.

Recovery from training accelerates during on-cycle weeks. Community consensus places noticeable recovery improvement at the 1 to 2 week mark, consistent with the IGF-1 elevation timeline from sustained GH pulsing.
Partially Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 18 key studies · Research only
Potent GHS-R1a agonist in human dose-response trials: about twice the GH release of GHRH at 1 mcg/kg IV [1].

Dosing studied: Phase I/II research SC: 1.5–3 mcg/kg per injection. Clinical trial ceiling effect at ~2 mcg/kg IV (~140 mcg/70 kg subject). No therapeutic SC RCT exists for the community 100-300 mcg range.

Reached Phase II clinical trials for adult GH deficiency and congestive heart failure (1990s); development discontinued, likely due to desensitization limiting long-term utility. Never FDA-approved. Rat heart studies found a distinct cardiac hexarelin receptor [2], later identified as CD36 [7]. Hexarelin protected rat hearts from ischemia/reperfusion injury, partly through GHS-R1a and, one group concluded, largely through CD36 [6] [8], not validated in human clinical endpoints. GH, prolactin, ACTH and cortisol rises matched GHRP-2 at equal IV doses in two small human studies [3] [9]. Head-to-head human data against GHRP-6 or ipamorelin are lacking. ~311 PubMed papers; the majority are mechanistic or short-term pharmacological studies, not therapeutic RCTs.
Key Study

Ghigo et al. 1994 (PMID 8126144): dose-response and route comparison in healthy men; established SC efficacy and dose ceiling. Bodart et al. 1999 (PMID 10532947): found a new 84 kDa cardiac hexarelin receptor that MK-0677 does not bind; Bodart et al. 2002 (PMID 11988484) identified it as CD36. Arvat et al. 1997 (PMID 9285939): in 6 healthy young adults, hexarelin and GHRP-2 at equal IV doses raised prolactin, ACTH and cortisol by similar amounts.
Limitations

No long-term therapeutic RCT for SC dosing. Desensitization mechanism documented in animals; formal human desensitization kinetics unpublished. Oral bioavailability ~0.3% (clinical trial data): not a practical route. SC bioavailability not formally quantified in humans (estimated 60-70% from mechanistic extrapolation). All cardioprotective data from animal models or in vitro: no human clinical endpoints confirmed.
Community Experience
Highly respected but niche and considered an advanced GHRP.
Community dosing: 100–200 mcg per injection SC, once or twice daily fasted

Strong consensus on it producing the largest GH pulse of any GHRP ("nothing else touches it for raw GH output") but most experienced users ultimately migrate to ipamorelin for long-term use due to cleaner hormonal profile and no desensitization. Hexarelin is reserved for short, intense cycles where maximum GH output is the priority. CD36 cardioprotective mechanism is frequently cited as a differentiator.

Science and community agree on GHS-R1a mechanism, a strong GH pulse, cortisol/prolactin elevation, and the principle of receptor desensitization requiring cycling. Community has independently converged on 4-week on/off cycling and the CJC-1295 no DAC stack: both mechanistically justified. Community SC dosing (100-300 mcg) extrapolates beyond any published clinical therapeutic RCT; 300 mcg 2×/day exceeds clinical dose-response ceiling. Science and community split on ranking. Community reports put hexarelin's GH pulse and its cortisol and prolactin rises above GHRP-2's. Two human studies at equal IV doses found all of them similar (PMID 9285939, 10195374). Community reports also treat CD36 as hexarelin's edge over other GHRPs; a 2017 review places CD36 binding across the GHRP family (PMID 28469491).
Community Community dosing consensus from peptide research communities

Stack hexarelin with a GHRH, not another GHRP. The single most common mistake is pairing it with ipamorelin or GHRP-2. Both hit the same GHS-R1a receptor. You're wasting one compound. The correct partner is CJC-1295 (no DAC) or sermorelin, co-injected simultaneously. Reconstitution math for a 5mg vial: add 2 mL bacteriostatic water. That gives you 2,500 mcg/mL. On a U-100 insulin syringe, 4 units equals 100 mcg, 8 units equals 200 mcg, 12 units equals 300 mcg. For a 2mg vial with 2 mL BAC water, you get 1,000 mcg/mL; 10 units equals 100 mcg. Fasting compliance matters more with hexarelin than most peptides. Carbohydrates and fats raise somatostatin, which blunts the GH pulse considerably. No food 30 minutes before or after injection at minimum. Two hours post-meal is better. If your IGF-1 isn't moving after 4 weeks, check your fasting window before blaming the product. Refrigerate reconstituted vials and use within 3 to 4 weeks.
Cycling Protocol
Off Period
Hexarelin desensitizes GHS receptors with continuous use. Cycle 4 weeks on, 2-4 weeks off to maintain GH responsiveness. Some protocols use 5 days on, 2 days off within each on-cycle week.
Hexarelin Cycle

Hexarelin has the highest GHS-R1a binding affinity of any GHRP. This high-affinity binding drives GHS-R1a downregulation and β-arrestin-mediated receptor internalization faster than any other peptide in this class. Desensitization of the GH pulse is the primary documented failure mode with continuous hexarelin use: onset typically within 4-6 weeks of daily dosing, with the community converging on a strict 4-week on / 2-4 week off protocol as the standard cycling approach. The 5-on/2-off within each week is a secondary mitigation strategy layered on top of the 4-week gross cycle. No long-term human receptor density data exists; the cycling rationale is mechanistically sound but the specific off-period duration is community convention rather than clinically validated.
Reduced post-injection warmth and tingling: a reliable early indicator that was present in the first 1-2 weeks and is now diminishing
Sleep improvement effect declining after weeks 3-4 of continuous dosing
IGF-1 plateauing or declining despite continued fasted protocol and correct dosing
Appetite stimulation post-injection becoming less pronounced (ghrelin pathway downregulating)

Reconstitute the vial For a 5mg vial, slowly inject 2 mL bacteriostatic water down the inside wall of the vial. Do not shake. Swirl gently until the powder dissolves completely. This gives you 2,500 mcg per mL.
Draw your dose using a U-100 insulin syringe (29-31 gauge, 0.5 inch needle). For 100 mcg, draw to the 4-unit mark. For 200 mcg, draw to 8 units. For 300 mcg, draw to 12 units.
Choose your injection site: abdomen (2 inches from the navel) or the fatty tissue on the outer thigh. Rotate sites with each injection.
Clean the injection site with an alcohol swab Pinch a fold of skin, insert the needle at a 45-degree angle, inject slowly, hold for 5 seconds, then withdraw.

Timing matters Best timing is 30 to 60 minutes before bed to amplify the natural nocturnal GH pulse. For twice-daily protocols, the morning dose should be on waking and fully fasted. Keep a minimum of 3 to 4 hours between injections.
If stacking with CJC-1295 (no DAC), draw both peptides into the same syringe and co-inject simultaneously. Do not pre-mix vials.
Store the reconstituted vial in the refrigerator at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Use within 3 to 4 weeks. Never freeze reconstituted solution.
Works With
CJC-1295 (No DAC) / Mod GRF 1-29

Primary and near-universal stack. GHRH (CJC-1295 no DAC) + GHRP (hexarelin) activates dual pituitary receptor pathways, GHRHR + GHS-R1a, producing a synergistic GH pulse significantly larger than either alone. Co-injected simultaneously to capture the synergistic window.
100 mcg CJC-1295 (no DAC) co-injected with 100-200 mcg hexarelin SC, once or twice daily, fasted
Sermorelin

Lower-cost alternative GHRH for the hexarelin stack. Shorter half-life than CJC-1295 (no DAC), otherwise similar synergistic mechanism via GHRHR activation. Preferred by users seeking lower cost or softer GHRH stimulus.
100-300 mcg sermorelin + 100-200 mcg hexarelin SC, co-injected, once or twice daily fasted
BPC-157

Concurrent tissue repair stack: separate mechanism from GH pathway. GH elevation from hexarelin complements BPC-157 angiogenic and healing signaling in injury recovery protocols. Often used in the intermediate/advanced cycle off-period or alongside.
Systemic recovery stack. TB-500 actin-binding and cell migration support combined with hexarelin GH-mediated anabolic signaling in injury and post-surgery recovery protocols.
Avoid
Ipamorelin

Both hexarelin and ipamorelin bind the same GHS-R1a receptor. Co-administration provides no additive GH benefit and accelerates receptor desensitization. Choose one GHRP and stack it with a GHRH peptide instead: the most common hexarelin mistake per community consensus.
GHRP-2

Same GHS-R1a receptor. Hexarelin already has the highest binding affinity of any GHRP. At equal doses, it and GHRP-2 raise cortisol and prolactin by similar amounts (PMID 9285939). Combining them compounds these side effects with no additional GH benefit from dual GHS-R1a occupancy.
GHRP-6
Same GHS-R1a receptor. Stacking hexarelin + GHRP-6 is redundant. GHRP-6 adds intense hunger stimulation and cortisol burden with no additive GH benefit over hexarelin alone.
Exogenous HGH (recombinant GH / somatropin)

Combining GH secretagogues with exogenous recombinant HGH saturates the GH/IGF-1 axis and suppresses endogenous pulsatility. Eliminates the primary rationale for secretagogue use. Dramatically increases IGF-1 overshoot risk.
Brand Price
No FDA-approved or branded pharmaceutical hexarelin product exists for human use. Never reached commercial approval.

Cortisol and prolactin elevation are the primary safety concerns with hexarelin. Community reports often rank it the worst GHRP for both. The human head-to-head tests against GHRP-2 don't back that ranking. Arvat's group gave both at equal IV doses in two small studies, and prolactin, ACTH and cortisol rose by similar amounts [3] [9]. At the beginner 100 mcg once daily dose, the cortisol bump is transient and typically returns to baseline within 2 to 3 hours post-injection. Rahim's group tracked cortisol in adults through 16 weeks of 1.5 mcg/kg twice daily, about 105 mcg at 70 kg [10]. The cortisol response to the morning injection was lower at week 16 than at baseline, and it recovered 4 weeks after stopping. The ACTH response, basal cortisol and 24-hour urinary free cortisol did not change. A one-day study in 6 young men found two or three injections left 24-hour cortisol, ACTH and prolactin output unchanged [11]. The aggressive 300 mcg twice daily protocol runs about three times Rahim's dose and lacks long-term data. Community reports at that dose describe disrupted sleep, irritability and shifts in fat distribution, which users blame on cortisol. Prolactin follows a similar dose-dependent pattern. At lower doses, the spike is brief and unlikely to produce symptoms. Over Rahim's 16 weeks of twice-daily dosing, the prolactin response did not change [10]. At higher twice-daily doses, community reports describe libido changes and, rarely, early gynecomastia signs. Checking prolactin at baseline and at week 4 is standard practice for anyone running intermediate or advanced protocols. Some users add low-dose cabergoline during aggressive cycles, though clinical backing for that approach in this context is thin. GHS-R1a receptor desensitization is not a side effect in the traditional sense, but it is the most common reason hexarelin "stops working." High-affinity binding drives beta-arrestin-mediated receptor internalization faster than GHRP-2, GHRP-6, or ipamorelin. The community figured this out before any formal study characterized the kinetics in humans. Four weeks of continuous daily dosing is the practical limit; beyond that, GH pulse magnitude drops noticeably. Receptor density recovers over 2 to 4 weeks off. Water retention and mild edema are common GH-class effects. At higher doses, fluid accumulation in the carpal tunnel can produce hand tingling, numbness, or grip weakness. These are early carpal tunnel symptoms. If they persist beyond a few days at a reduced dose, stopping the cycle entirely and allowing 4 or more weeks for resolution is the right call. Appetite increase occurs through the ghrelin pathway. It's less intense than GHRP-6, but still present, especially at 200 mcg and above. This can actually disrupt the fasting window required for proper dosing if not managed. Shifting the bedtime dose to 3 or more hours after dinner helps. Post-injection flushing and tingling within 10 to 20 minutes is a GH flush effect and is harmless. It's actually a useful signal: when the flush stops appearing in later weeks, it often indicates desensitization has begun. Hexarelin has not been studied in pregnant or breastfeeding individuals. GH and IGF-1 elevation carry theoretical risks for fetal development and should be avoided entirely. Anyone with active malignancy, pituitary tumors, intracranial hypertension, or uncontrolled diabetes should not use hexarelin. GH elevation impairs glucose tolerance and may promote tumor growth through the IGF-1 axis. When to see a doctor: persistent carpal tunnel symptoms beyond one week, fasting glucose climbing above 125 mg/dL, any signs of prolactin elevation (libido changes, breast tissue changes), or edema that doesn't resolve with dose reduction.
Common Issues & Solutions

No IGF-1 movement after 4-6 weeks: Most common cause is eating within 30-60 min before/after injection: carbohydrates and fats raise somatostatin and blunt the GH pulse significantly. Verify fasting compliance before questioning product quality or dosing.

GH response decreasing week over week ("hexarelin stopped working"): Classic GHS-R1a desensitization. Implement 5-on/2-off weekly schedule immediately; if already past 4 weeks continuous, stop for at least 2 weeks minimum (4 preferred) before resuming. Receptor sensitivity typically restores within 2-4 weeks off.

Hand tingling, numbness, or grip weakness: Early carpal tunnel symptoms from GH-mediated fluid retention in the carpal tunnel. Reduce dose or injection frequency immediately. If symptoms persist beyond 1 week at lower dose, discontinue and allow 4+ weeks for GH-related edema to resolve.

Sleep disrupted despite bedtime dosing or cortisol-like symptoms (fat gain, irritability): Hexarelin raises ACTH and cortisol about as much as GHRP-2 does at equal doses [3]. At aggressive doses (300 mcg 2×/day) this is clinically relevant. Check AM cortisol; consider dose reduction or switching to ipamorelin for subsequent cycles.

Post-injection intense hunger: Less than GHRP-6 but still present: particularly at higher doses. This is a ghrelin-pathway side effect. If hunger disrupts fasting compliance, shift bedtime dose later (post-dinner, 3+ hours fasted) or consider switching to ipamorelin for cleaner dosing.

Hexarelin is a 6-amino-acid synthetic peptide (MW ~888 Da): synthesis is relatively straightforward for established peptide manufacturers. No GMP requirement applies to "research use only" peptide products. The compound is genuine GH axis-active; underdosed or impure product produces a measurably blunted IGF-1 response (objectively testable). Hexarelin has never received FDA approval for any indication. It reached Phase II clinical trials in the 1990s for GH deficiency and congestive heart failure, but development was discontinued before any regulatory submission. It is currently classified as a research-only compound in the United States. Hexarelin is not on FDA's 503A bulk drug substances list (21 CFR 216.23), and FDA has not placed it in any compounding category. It is absent from the 503A category lists (updated May 14, 2026) and the 503B category list (updated March 21, 2025). It was not part of the 2026 Category 2 changes or the July 2026 advisory committee meeting. The compound is sold online as a "for research use only" product. WADA prohibits all growth hormone releasing peptides, including hexarelin, under Section S2 (Peptide Hormones, Growth Factors, Related Substances and Mimetics). Athletes subject to anti-doping testing should not use this compound. This content is for informational purposes only. Hexarelin is not approved for human therapeutic use. Consult a qualified healthcare provider before considering any peptide protocol.

phases.name: Ramp-in
phases.syringeUnits: 10 units (2mg vial + 2mL BAC water = 1,000 mcg/mL) OR 4 units (5mg vial + 2mL BAC water = 2,500 mcg/mL)
phases.timing: 30-60 min before bed, minimum 30 min fasted (ideally 2+ hours post-meal)
phases.notes: Start once daily bedtime to assess tolerance. Co-inject CJC-1295 (no DAC) 100 mcg simultaneously for synergistic GHRH + GHRP GH pulse. Assess for hunger, flushing, and tingling. Do NOT stack with any second GHRP (ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6): same GHS-R1a receptor.

phases.name: Maintenance
phases.frequency: Once daily (bedtime), 5 days on / 2 days off each week
phases.syringeUnits: 4 units per injection (5mg vial + 2mL BAC water = 2,500 mcg/mL)
phases.notes: Implement 5-on/2-off within each week to slow GHS-R1a desensitization. Cycle off after 4 weeks total. Do not extend beyond 4 weeks without a minimum 2-week break.

protocols.monitoringNotes: Baseline IGF-1 before starting; recheck at week 4. Fasting glucose at baseline.

protocols.goal: Body recomposition / short cycle GH output

phases.name: Full Cycle
phases.frequency: Twice daily (AM fasted + bedtime), 5 days on / 2 days off each week
phases.syringeUnits: 8 units per injection (5mg vial + 2mL BAC water = 2,500 mcg/mL)
phases.timing: AM: on waking fasted; PM: 30-60 min before bed fasted; minimum 3-4h between injections
phases.notes: Co-inject CJC-1295 (no DAC) 100 mcg at each hexarelin injection for synergistic GHRH + GHRP pulse. 200 mcg is the practical community ceiling per injection. Strict 4-week cap mandatory: receptor desensitization is the primary failure mode at this frequency.

protocols.monitoringNotes: Baseline IGF-1, fasting glucose, prolactin. Recheck IGF-1 at week 4. Monitor blood glucose in pre-diabetic individuals.

protocols.goal: Maximum GH pulse: advanced short cycle

phases.name: High-dose Cycle
phases.frequency: Twice daily (AM fasted + post-workout or bedtime), 5 days on / 2 days off each week
phases.syringeUnits: 12 units per injection (5mg vial + 2mL BAC water = 2,500 mcg/mL)
phases.timing: AM fasted; post-workout (minimum 20 min post-exercise, no food); minimum 4h between injections
phases.notes: 300 mcg 2×/day (600 mcg/day total) exceeds all published clinical trial doses and the documented GHS-R1a dose-response ceiling (~140 mcg for a 70 kg individual). Community uses this dose for maximal GH pulse in 4-week blasts but diminishing GH returns per injection are likely. Significantly increased cortisol and prolactin burden vs. lower doses. Not recommended without prior experience at intermediate level. 4-week cap is non-negotiable: desensitization accelerates rapidly at this dose and frequency. Follow with at least 4 weeks off.

protocols.monitoringNotes: Full baseline panel: IGF-1, IGFBP-3, fasting glucose, HbA1c, AM cortisol, prolactin, thyroid (TSH, fT3, fT4). Recheck at week 4. Do not restart without confirming IGF-1 return toward baseline.

faqs.q: Why does hexarelin need cycling when other GHRPs don't?
faqs.a: Hexarelin binds GHS-R1a with higher affinity than GHRP-2, GHRP-6, or ipamorelin, and that means more receptor downregulation with continuous use. Desensitization typically sets in after 4-6 weeks of daily dosing, noticeably reducing your GH pulse. A 2-4 week off period lets receptor density recover.

faqs.q: Can I stack hexarelin with ipamorelin for a bigger GH pulse?
faqs.a: No, this is one of the most common mistakes. Both compete for the same GHS-R1a receptor. Taking both doesn't amplify anything; it wastes one compound. The correct stack is hexarelin (or any single GHRP) with a GHRH like Mod GRF 1-29 or sermorelin, different receptor pathways that actually synergize.

faqs.q: Is the cortisol and prolactin elevation a real problem?
faqs.a: At beginner doses (100 mcg/day), it's mild and usually not clinically significant. At aggressive doses (300 mcg 2x/day), community reports describe poorer sleep and stalled fat loss, though that dose lacks long-term data. In a 16-week trial in adults at 1.5 mcg/kg twice daily, the cortisol response fell and the prolactin response did not change (PMID 10341859). Some users add vitamin C, ashwagandha, or low-dose cabergoline during cycles, though that adds complexity without strong clinical backing.

faqs.q: Was hexarelin ever in real clinical trials?
faqs.a: It reached Phase II trials for GH deficiency and congestive heart failure in the 1990s. Development stopped. Not because of safety failures, but likely because the desensitization issue limited long-term use, and the competitive market moved on. Never submitted for FDA approval.

faqs.q: Are the cardioprotective effects real at bodybuilding doses?
faqs.a: Hexarelin binds the CD36 scavenger receptor on heart cells independently of GH release, producing anti-fibrotic effects and preserved contractility during ischemia. These effects show up in animal models at doses that extrapolate to the 100-200 mcg human range. Whether that benefit translates to healthy individuals (rather than ischemic models) is unknown.
Hexarelin typically comes in 2mg or 5mg vials. Add 2mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Hexarelin?
faqs.a: The half-life of Hexarelin is ~70 min. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.
